rec_smoking_rationale: Tobacco smoke damages blood vessels and speeds up atherosclerosis. After one year without smoking, the excess risk of coronary heart disease falls by about half (US Surgeon General's report, 1990).
rec_smoking_action: Consult a specialist for a structured smoking cessation or nicotine replacement protocol.
rec_bp_title: Blood Pressure Optimization to Target Range
rec_bp_rationale: ESC/ESH 2018 and WHO 2021 recommend target BP < 130/80 mmHg to prevent myocardial infarction and stroke.
rec_bp_action: Limit dietary sodium (< 5 g/day), maintain a BP home log, and adjust antihypertensive therapy with a physician.
rec_lipids_rationale: A 20% reduction in total cholesterol stabilizes atherosclerotic plaques and cuts 10-year vascular events.
rec_lipids_action: Adopt a cardioprotective dietary pattern rich in soluble fiber and unsaturated fats; discuss statin therapy if indicated.
rec_weight_rationale: A 5–10% weight loss improves hemodynamics, decreases insulin resistance, and attenuates vascular inflammation.
rec_weight_action: Engage in 150–300 min/week of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise alongside a modest caloric deficit.
rec_glucose_rationale: Elevated fasting glucose accelerates vascular end-glycation products and micro/macrovascular damage.
rec_glucose_action: Obtain an HbA1c test and consult an endocrinologist for early metabolic evaluation.
rec_maintenance_optimal: All clinical biomarkers are within optimal target ranges. Continue an active lifestyle with biannual screenings.

about_sec_1_title: 1. Relevance of the Problem in Uzbekistan
about_sec_1_text:
- **The leading cause of death.** In 2024, 112,482 people in Uzbekistan died of cardiovascular disease (World Heart Federation, World Heart Observatory).
- **A silent disease.** High blood pressure and cholesterol go unnoticed for years — until a heart attack or stroke.
- **Little time in the consulting room.** A primary-care doctor rarely has time to work out a risk score by hand and explain what matters most to change.
about_sec_2_text:
**Yurak** is a domestic digital assistant for cardiovascular risk screening and personalized longevity, developed within a student startup initiative.

**Core Technological Advantages:**
1. **Explainable AI (XAI):** The AI model avoids «black-box» opacity. **Integrated Gradients** transparently reveals the exact contribution of each clinical biomarker in percentage points.
2. **Two-Tier Hybrid Architecture:**
   - *Clinical guideline thresholds* (WHO, ESC/ESH 2018) identify disease risk factors.
   - *The AI model* simulates actionable counterfactuals ($\Delta$ risk reduction, vascular rejuvenation) and ranks steps by maximum clinical utility.
3. **Tailored for Uzbekistan:** Integration of official WHO Life Tables for the Republic of Uzbekistan (2023) and native Uzbek (Latin script) language support.
4. **International Interoperability:** Native export in **HL7 FHIR R4** standard, fully ready for integration with hospital Electronic Medical Records (EMR).

meth_cohort_desc:
**Training Cohort:** Framingham Heart Study (publicly verified teaching cohort of the US National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute — NHLBI).
- **Total Sample Size:** 4,240 participants, 16 baseline clinical features.
- **Stratified Split:** 70% Train (2,968), 15% Validation (636), 15% Test (636).
- **Test Outcome Prevalence:** 10-year CHD incident — **15.25%**, diabetes — **2.83%**.
- **Preprocessing:** Missing values imputed via train medians, standardization (Z-score).
- **Clinical Limitation:** Reflects the Framingham population. Local calibration is required for clinical practice in Uzbekistan.
meth_clinical_desc:
**1. Vascular Heart Age Formula (D'Agostino et al., Circulation 2008):**
Strict analytical closed-form formula based on Cox proportional hazards:
$$\text{Heart Age} = \exp\left(\frac{L_{\text{patient}} - C_{\text{ref}}}{\beta_{\text{age}}}\right)$$
For an optimal profile of any age, it is proven that: $\text{Heart Age} \equiv \text{Chronological Age}$.

**2. Life Expectancy Estimation via WHO Uzbekistan Mortality Tables (2023):**
$$\text{Life Expectancy} = \text{Age} + e_x(\text{Heart Age})$$
where $e_x$ is remaining life expectancy derived from official WHO GHO mortality tables for Uzbekistan.
meth_limits_desc:
- **Lack of Local Cohort Studies:** Trained on the US Framingham cohort. Full deployment in Uzbekistan requires a local clinical validation study.
- **Lipid Panel Specifics:** The public teaching cohort provides total cholesterol without direct LDL-C fractions or triglycerides.
- **Screening Scope:** Designed for risk stratification and health literacy, not for replacing clinical physician diagnosis.

ov_lead: In a minute, free, no sign-up. All you need is your height, weight, blood pressure and how much you smoke; blood tests make it more accurate but aren't required. Yurak shows your heart age, your 10-year risk, and which steps would lower it most.
meth_sec_inputs: What we ask for, and why
meth_inputs_desc:
Every field changes at least one result. Each effect was checked on the model by moving the marker from a typical low to a typical high value.

| What you enter | What it affects |
|---|---|
| Age, sex | everything |
| Upper pressure, BP pills | heart risk, heart age |
| Lower pressure | heart risk (weakly) |
| Height and weight (BMI) | heart risk, diabetes risk; heart age when cholesterol is missing |
| Total cholesterol (optional) | heart risk, heart age |
| HDL (optional) | heart age |
| Fasting glucose (optional) | heart risk, diabetes risk; from 7.0 mmol/L counts as diabetes in heart age |
| Diabetes diagnosis | heart age |
| Cigarettes a day | heart risk (by amount), heart age (smoker or not) |
| Early heart disease in the family | not in the formulas; adds a note for the doctor |

**Without blood tests.** Heart age uses the second model from the same D'Agostino (2008) paper, where BMI replaces cholesterol; the network gets typical values from the training data — the same way missing values were filled during training.

**Who it's not for.** People after a heart attack or stroke, and people under 32 or over 70: instead of numbers they get an explanation and their markers next to the normal ranges.

**Alarming values.** Blood pressure from 180/110, glucose from 7.0 mmol/L without a diagnosis, cholesterol from 7.5 mmol/L and BMI from 40 get a separate warning before any number.

**Removed:** resting heart rate (moved risk by < 1.6 pp, in the wrong direction) and stroke as a risk-factor question.

**Life expectancy** isn't on the main screen: it's a rough estimate from WHO tables. Instead it shows how many years the steps could add.
unit_hint: Check the units on your lab report.
section_lab_hint: Optional. No blood test? Leave these empty — the check still works.
field_family_history: My father or brother had a heart attack or stroke before 55, or my mother or sister before 65
field_family_history_help: Early cardiovascular disease in the family is a recognised risk factor (ESC). It isn't in the formula, but it changes the advice.
family_history_note: An early heart attack or stroke in close relatives raises your risk beyond the calculated value — the calculator can't account for it. Be sure to tell your doctor.
age_out_body: The model was trained on people aged 32–70, so a risk number for your age would be a guess. Below are your markers next to the normal ranges — worth discussing with a doctor.
heart_age_bmi_note: Cholesterol wasn't entered, so heart age uses D'Agostino's simplified formula, where body mass index replaces the blood test. With cholesterol the result is more accurate.
card_gain_help: How much the life-expectancy estimate rises if you do every step below. Based on WHO tables for Uzbekistan and heart age — a reference point, not a promise.
card_dm_unknown_help: Diabetes risk needs a fasting glucose value.
next_low: Your risk is low. Keep your habits: at least 150 minutes of moderate activity a week (WHO), less salt, no tobacco. Check your blood pressure at least once a year and redo this check if your numbers change.
next_mid: Your risk is intermediate. Book your family doctor within the next few weeks: show them the PDF report and get cholesterol and glucose tested if you haven't. Start with the first step below — it helps most.
next_high: Your risk is high. See a doctor soon — don't put it off. Take the PDF report: your doctor will decide whether you need medicine for blood pressure or cholesterol. The steps below help but don't replace treatment.
next_urgent: Your blood pressure is in the danger zone. Rest 5 minutes and measure again. If it's still 180/110 or higher, see a doctor today. If you also have chest pain, a headache, or trouble seeing or speaking, call 103.
labs_missing_note: Without blood tests the risk is approximate: typical values were used instead. Total cholesterol and fasting glucose would make it more accurate.
alert_bp_severe: Blood pressure of 180/110 or higher is very high (grade 3 hypertension, ESC/ESH). Don't delay seeing a doctor.
alert_glucose_diabetic: Fasting glucose of 7.0 mmol/L or higher is in the diabetic range. It needs confirming with a doctor: a repeat test and HbA1c.
alert_chol_very_high: Total cholesterol of 7.5 mmol/L or higher is very high. Discuss a full lipid panel and treatment with your doctor.
alert_bmi_severe: A body mass index of 40 or higher is class III obesity (WHO). Worth discussing a weight-loss plan with a doctor.
emergency_title: Signs of a heart attack or stroke — when to call 103
emergency_body:
- Chest pain, pressure or burning lasting more than a few minutes, especially spreading to the arm, neck or jaw.
- Sudden shortness of breath, cold sweat, nausea, weakness.
- A drooping face, weakness in an arm or leg, slurred speech — signs of a stroke.

**Call 103** (ambulance in Uzbekistan). Don't wait for it to pass, and don't drive yourself.
privacy_note: Yurak doesn't ask for your name or phone number and doesn't store what you enter: the check lives only in the open tab.
ov_need_body: Height and weight. Blood pressure — you can measure it at home or at a pharmacy. Cigarettes a day. If you have a recent blood test: total cholesterol and fasting glucose.
